goal: A reviewer opens a feature's run page to see every claim the user decided on for that feature, the regressions that were run, and the recorded video for each.

properties.statement: Every claim the user decided on for the current feature shows in the Intent section, with its own card.

read_as.applies_to: Claims the user decided on (confirmed) for the current feature, as listed in the Intent section of the run review page
read_as.action: Render the Intent list: one card per journey/claim, showing the feature's claims
read_as.compares: Reference: the feature's claims/journeys (T.claims, T.journeys); compared with the cards rendered in the Intent list

properties.how_found: Plain code searched the codebase for \bjourneys\b, claimIds (the journeys list rendered as cards in the Intent pane (journeys filtered to those with a replay, with their claim chips)), then for the name of each function that changes it, then for the address of each route that reaches it, and followed every file that mentions one up to the pages. 2 search hits were each labelled by their own model call. This gave 1 way(s) in through the pages and 0 route(s); 0 file(s) were excluded because no page shows them.
properties.not_covered: I did not plan cases for a feature with zero claims or for claims marked recorded-only. Only one feature (shopping-cart) exists, and the run page rendered blank when I observed it, so I could not confirm those situations. No direct API cases were planned because none were listed. The route list was empty and I could not read the page's behaviour in the browser.

ways_in.where: The run review page for a feature (reached from the Test runs list at /runs, then the feature's run, e.g. shopping-cart). Its Intent section is a list with one card per journey, showing the journey name, a thumbnail and claim chips. Opening /review/run.html directly showed only 'not found'. The run page itself rendered blank when I observed it.

search_notes: 20 lines mention the journeys list rendered as cards in the Intent pane (journeys filtered to those with a replay, with their claim chips) without writing it (as far as plain code can tell); they were not followed.
The name feature appears on 268 lines, too many to follow by search; its callers were not traced.

cases.what: Open /runs and note the shopping-cart row, which says 3 claims, 2 journeys and 2 of 3 verified. Open that run's review page. Find the Intent section and count its cards. Read each card's name and the claim chips on it. Compare these with the feature's confirmed claims: every claim should show on some card, each journey should have its own card, and no claim should be missing or duplicated.
cases.stands_for: Basic wiring: the Intent list renders one card per journey, showing the feature's claims.
cases.observed: /runs shows shopping-cart: 3 claims, 2 journeys, 2 checks, 2 of 3 verified. The run page /runs/shopping-cart has an Intent filter button with count 2 and Regression 0. The Intent list has 2 cards. Both are named "Items go into the cart" (0:07 and 0:08), one with chip C1 (Verified) and one with chip C2 (Verified). No card or chip shows a third claim (C3), and no card shows a second distinct journey name. So 3 claims and 2 journeys are expected, but only 2 claims show, so one claim is missing from the Intent list. Screenshot: shot-1.

cases.stands_for: Basic wiring: clicking a card selects it and loads its own video.
cases.observed: /review/run.html and /review/ showed only "not found". I opened the run from /runs and went to /runs/shopping-cart, which lists 2 cards: C1 and C2. Before the click, the visible player was already on /runs/shopping-cart/videos/c1.webm. I clicked the first card (C1, "Items go into the cart 0:07"). After the click, the visible player source was /runs/shopping-cart/videos/c1.webm (6.88 s). The hidden players held c1.webm and c2.webm. C1's own recorded video is c1.webm, so they match. The C1 claim detail was shown. C1 was probably already selected before my click, so this does not prove the click itself changed the source. I did not click C2 and then C1. Screenshot: shot-1.
